clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. The Director of the International Communication Agency is  
designated and empowered to perform the functions conferred upon the  
President by the above-mentioned Act and shall be deemed to be authorized,  
without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, (1) to  
determine that any work of art or other object to be imported into the United  
States within the meaning of the Act is of cultural significance, (2) to deter­
mine that the temporary exhibition or display of any such work of art or other  
object in the United States is in the national interest, and (3) to cause public  
notices of the determinations referred to above to be published in the Feder­
al R egister.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. The Director of the International Communication Agency, in  
carrying out this Order, shall consult with the Secretary of State with respect  
to the determination of national interest, and may consult with the Secretary  
of the Smithsonian Institution, the Director of the National Gallery of Art, and  
with such other officers and agencies of the Government as may be appropri­
ate, with respect to the determination of cultural significance.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. The Director of the International Communication Agency is au­
thorized to delegate within the Agency the functions conferred upon him by  
this Order.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text: Sec. 4. Executive Order No. 11312 of October 14, 1966 is revoked.

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text:
Sec. 5. Any order, regulation, determination or other action which was in  
effect pursuant to the provisions of Executive Order No. 11312 shall remain in  
effect until changed pursuant to the authority provided in this Order.

clauses.label: Sec. 6.
clauses.text: Sec. 6. This Order shall be effective on April 1, 1978.

record.reasoning: Identity (EO 12047, 1978-03-27, Carter, 43 FR 13359, filed 1978-03-28, printed 1978-03-29), the six-clause inventory, all quotes and hashes check out. The operative analysis of secs 1, 2, 3 and 5 is supported: EO 12388 (effective as of 1982-08-24) only substitutes the agency name, the 22 U.S.C. 2459 note lists no other amendment, the FR note shows only the EO 12388 amendment and the EO 11312 revocation, no held order text revokes it, and the 2026-10-02 State Department notice makes the sec 1 determinations under EO 12047. versions.research_rationale:
EO 12047 (signed 1978-03-27, Jimmy Carter; 43 FR 13359, filed 1978-03-28, printed 1978-03-29) designates the director of the foreign-information agency to exercise the President's functions under the Act of October 19, 1965 (79 Stat. 985, 22 U.S.C. 2459) on imported objects of cultural significance. I read the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12047.txt in full: the preamble and sections 1 through 6 are all present, the six prepared inventory clauses cover every operative section, and identity (number, title, date, signer, page) matches the register row. Later instruments: EO 12388 (signed 1982-10-14, 47 FR 46245; effective as of August 24, 1982 under its section 6) amends sections 1, 2 and 3 only by substituting the agency name; it is the only later order in the held Federal Register disposition notes and the number search of held texts (the other citing texts are the 1989 codification snapshot and a 2026 Department of State notice). The 2026-10-02 notice (91 FR 62802) is current-use evidence that determinations under section 1 are still made in reliance on this order. The U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected) found a note under 22 U.S.C. 2459 printing the order, and the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) was read for coverage; neither records a revocation. Sections 4 and 6 are terminated by performance on 1978-04-01; sections 1, 2, 3 and 5 are operative.
